newsitem.title: ITALY: Biblical language plagues interpreter at summit.
newsitem.headline: Biblical language plagues interpreter at summit.

text.p: U.N. bureaucrats could have used the wisdom of Solomon on Thursday when a speech in Hebrew by an Israeli minister to a World Food Summit was interrupted because an interpreter couldn't handle the Biblical language.

Agriculture and Environment Minister Rafael Eitan was reading his speech in Hebrew from the podium while a silmultaneous interpreter in a glass booth was reading a translation that had been prepared in English.
But then a technical glitch cut off the minister from the interpreter, who fell behind as Eitan carried.
The exasperated interpreter interrupted: "If the interpreter could just apologise to the minister and the chairman.

"It's being read in Hebrew and the interpreter does not understand Hebrew and he is being led through the text in English. We are trying to find exactly where the speaker is in the text that is in front of the interpreter."
The U.N.-spopnsored summit came to a halt for several minutes as bewildered officials mulled how to handle what was fast becoming a diplomatic embarrassment.
Then the acting chairman apologized profusely and asked the minister and the interpreter to just start all over again.
Before he resumed the minister -- this time speaking in clear and understandable English -- joked that Hebrew was one of the world's oldest languages.
It wasn't the first time there was a "misunderstanding" between a speaker and an interpreter.

On Wednesday, an announcement heard through the English interpreter said: "The secretariat has...been informed that the statement of the government of the Philippines will be delivered by His Excellency Leticia Ramos-Shahani."
Ramos-Shahani, who is mounting a campaign to succeed Boutros Boutros-Ghali as U.N. secretary-general, is a woman.
